slides.title: Se... então
slides.text: A primeira condicional fala de possibilidades reais: 'If it rains, we'll stay home.' Depois de 'if', use o presente simples. No resultado, use will + verbo.
Eva e Max planejam o fim de semana com base no clima.
slides.line: What are we doing this weekend, Eva?

slides.title: Weekend plans
slides.text: Eva and Max have two plans for the weekend. If it's sunny, they'll go to the beach and swim. If it rains, they'll stay home, cook and watch movies. Eva checks the weather forecast every hour. "If it rains, I'll make a cake," she says. "If you bring ice cream, I'll share it," says Max. On Saturday morning, the sun comes out and they pack their bags. They arrive at the beach at ten. "Plan A wins!" says Eva. They run into the water. It is a perfect day.
slides.pt: Eva e Max têm dois planos, e o sol decide: praia!

slides.title: O clima inglês
slides.text: O clima na Inglaterra é famoso por mudar de hora em hora. Por isso, os ingleses sempre dizem: 'If it rains…, if it doesn't…'. Levar um guarda-chuva é regra: 'Be prepared'.
